technical_and_design_decisions: Spring XD is the target platform for the software increment, given references to custom modules, xd/lib, HDFS-hosted modules, and stream sinks.
The native WebSocket sink will be implemented using Spring Framework's WebSocket support (Spring messaging over STOMP or raw WebSocket) and integrate with Spring XD's Sink module SPI.
Uber-jar packaging for custom modules will use the Gradle shadow plugin (or equivalent) to bundle all transitive dependencies into a single deployable jar suitable for HDFS placement.

HDFS hosting will leverage the existing Hadoop FileSystem client configuration used by Spring XD, with the admin REST API extended (or a deployment script added) to push the uber-jar to the XD_HOME directory on HDFS.
CI improvements will be implemented as Gradle task and Bamboo plan configuration changes; no application code changes are expected for U4 and most of U5.
PMD/Sonar violations will be addressed primarily by fixing code issues, supplemented by SonarQube notification configuration (e.g., webhook/email to committers).
Windows CI setup will use the Bamboo agent's PowerShell capability and Windows-native service start commands for redis, rabbit, etc.

The shared jar location (U8) will be implemented as a documented convention backed by the Spring XD classloader hierarchy (xd/lib precedence) rather than a runtime change, with version-conflict mitigation via module-local shading when necessary.
assumptions: The developer is familiar with Spring XD, Spring Framework, Gradle, Bamboo, and the Hadoop HDFS client APIs.
The CI infrastructure (Bamboo, EC2 agents, Artifactory, SonarQube) already exists and is accessible; only configuration changes are required.
Existing custom module samples are available to serve as templates for the HDFS-hosted uber-jar work.
WARN log noise is caused by a manageable set of recurring issues (estimated <30 distinct sites) rather than pervasive misuse of logging APIs.
PMD/Sonar violations are similar in scope (estimated <50 violations), with a typical remediation cost of 15-30 minutes each.
The Windows CI agent already has JDK, Gradle, and required SDKs installed; setup work is limited to service configuration and task wiring.
Unit and integration tests already exist for the affected modules; new tests are added for the new WebSocket sink and HDFS deployment flow.
No new third-party commercial dependencies are introduced; everything is implemented with open-source libraries already in the project's stack.
A single developer performs all work; no hand-off, coordination, or stakeholder meeting overhead is included beyond what is implicit in the activities.
Effort is expressed in ideal work-hours of focused development (no time off for meetings, training, or unrelated work).

activities.activity_description: Analyze all eight user stories, identify affected Spring XD subsystems, define module SPI extensions for the WebSocket sink, design the HDFS deployment flow, and document the overall technical approach for the increment.

Author/update documentation covering how to build a custom module as an uber-jar, recommended coding patterns, packaging conventions, and deployment instructions. Includes a worked example and review with the team.

Configure Gradle shadow/uber-jar build for custom modules, implement the script/API to upload the uber-jar to HDFS (xd/lib equivalent on the cluster), and verify that newly arriving containers can resolve and load the module via the existing distribution mechanism.

Implement a new Spring XD sink module that uses native WebSocket APIs (Spring WebSocket) for full-duplex communication. Includes module metadata, option validation, client/server mode handling, payload mapping, error handling, and unit tests.

Investigate npm-cache as a candidate for caching node/npm dependencies between CI builds, evaluate alternatives, document trade-offs, and produce a recommendation. Implementation of the chosen solution is assumed to be handled in a follow-up by the build team.

Enable distributed JVM tests in the Gradle build, switch from the Artifactory Gradle plugin task to a command task invoking ./gradlew, disable embedded Hadoop in CI, and turn on maxParallelForks. Validate build stability on the EC2 agents.

activities.activity_name: PMD/Sonar WARN log investigation and fixes (U6)
activities.activity_description: Investigate the root cause of increased WARN-level log output, triage and fix the underlying issues, remediate PMD and SonarQube violations, and configure SonarQube (e.g., webhook/email) to notify committers of new violations on commit.

Configure a Bamboo build plan that runs on the existing Windows environment with PowerShell access, install and start required services (Redis, RabbitMQ, etc.), and wire up a commit-triggered CI task that executes the integration test suite on Windows.

Define and document the convention for placing shared jars under xd/lib, update build scripts as needed to populate this directory, and provide guidance (with classloader-level examples) for handling version conflicts by bundling the alternate version inside the custom module.

Write or extend unit tests for the WebSocket sink, HDFS deployment flow, PMD/Sonar fixes, and any code changes introduced for the CI improvements. Maintain or improve code coverage on touched modules.

Run end-to-end integration tests on Linux (existing suite) and Windows (new suite) to validate the WebSocket sink against a live broker, the HDFS module distribution flow against a real HDFS cluster, and the shared jar convention with multi-module deployment scenarios.
Self-review and refactor the changes, update CHANGELOG/release notes, verify Bamboo plans are green, and prepare the increment for merge/release.
